# odyssey-100 (Odyssey 20.199–298) — review, pass 1

Reviewer pass 1 of 2. `gloss.json` was not yet present and was not read; the second pass checks it.
Files read: runbook §2, conventions.md (rules sections in full; the house-renderings table searched
form by form for every word of this part, not read row by row), packet.md, units.json,
new-renderings.md, odyssey-001/units.json (model), the last units of odyssey-099.json, parts.json.
All edits were made by script (`units.json`, never `t`; `t` re-checked afterwards: unchanged, and
joined it still equals the packet's text). Scansion flags in the packet: none, so no line was scanned
by hand and no metrical sentence was added. No line-numbering irregularity falls in this part.

Mechanical checks that passed: 60 units; `p` on exactly the 14 paragraph starts (199, 226, 238, 240,
245, 247, 257, 262, 268, 271, 275, 279, 284, 292); `l` has the same `\n` count as `t`; no `\n` in `i`;
seven speeches, each with “ on the first unit and `mark` there (199 Philoetius speaks, 227 Odysseus
answers, 236 Philoetius answers, 245 Amphinomus speaks, 262 Telemachus speaks, 271 Antinous speaks,
292 Ctesippus speaks) and ” on the last unit (224/225, 233/234, 236/237, 246, 266/267, 273b/274, 296–298), in
both `l` and `i`. Speech continuity: odyssey-099 ends on the introduction of Philoetius's greeting
(197, “spoke winged words to him:”), so the opening “ at 199 is right. Repeated lines: 20.207, 226,
230–231, 239, 240, 247, 249, 256, 268, 270, 279–280, 283 all carry the published `l`/`i`
(whole-unit ones identical; partial ones reuse the published wording). The new renderings in
new-renderings.md are applied as listed.

a house rendering broken, or `l`/`i` out of step in sense or force; **minor** = wording, an
unsupported remark, a typo.

## Findings considered and refused (with reason)

- **201 `l` "none of the gods is deadlier than you, none other"**: the doubled "none" looks redundant, but it renders οὔ τις … ἄλλος faithfully in Greek order and agrees with `i` and note. Kept.
- **224 `l`/`i` "I have in mind" / "think of" for ὀΐομαι**: ὀΐομαι is "suppose, expect" and here takes an accusative with an εἰ-clause; the note says the construction is loose and glosses both ways. The three layers agree with each other. Kept.
- **222 note on ὑπερμενής "can carry a tone of arrogance"**: looked unsupported, but it is the house note carried by the table row for 19.62. Kept.
- **245 συνθεύσεται "run along" / "will not go well"**: the sense is a guess from context; the note says so ("taken from the context"). Kept; the second pass may reconsider "run along" against συν-.
- **262 `i` "drinking your wine"**: "your" is not in the Greek, but it is the natural English for the wine just poured for him (260). Kept.
- **263 vs 267 `i` "the hands of all the suitors" / "from blows"**: χειρῶν is rendered differently in the two lines. 263's "hands" is the object-noun with κερτομίας; 267's "blows" is the sense the note now states. Left as a deliberate gloss, now documented in the 266 note; flagged for the owner if strict identity is wanted.
- **268 note "marvelling" beside `l` "marveled"**: spelling difference between a note and a layer that carries the published wording. Kept; the layer cannot change.
- **255 note "Μελανθεύς is the same man as Μελάνθιος"**: a statement about the rest of the poem, but the table already ships Μελάνθιος (17.247, 17.369) and the English name in both layers is Melanthius. Kept.
- **199 `i` "Welcome, stranger, my father" and the 199 `l`**: match the table row for πάτερ ὦ ξεῖνε exactly. Kept.
- **235/291/226/230/239/240/247/249/256/268/270/279/283**: repeated-line wording checked against the packet; no divergence.
- **The packet flagged no scansion irregularity**; nothing to scan, no sentence added.
- **Greek → `l`, case/tense/mood/particle pass**: every unit read; no further mistranslation found beyond the table above. Points checked and found sound: γένοιτο opt. of wish; ἔχεαι pass.; ἐπόψεαι fut.; αἴ κ’ ἐθέλῃσθα; γνοίης χ’ potential; εἴασε; παύσαμεν with κε; θείῃ subj.; ὄρηται; δύη; δῶ/δώῃ; κέκλυτε; ἐνώμων/νεῖμε/ἐπένειμε; ἐῳνοχόει; ἀνώγει.
- **Remembered English**: the one phrase suspected of arriving fully formed was "bring this word to pass" (changed, above). The rest was rebuilt from the grammar and the table; nothing else read as borrowed.

## Findings considered and refused (with reason)

- **227 ἄφρονι "foolish" / κακῷ "bad"**: the table row for ἄφρων (17.586) fixes "senseless", and
  κακός of a person is "base" in the row for 9.453/10.301. But the identical half-line
  ἐπεὶ οὔτε κακῷ οὔτ’ ἄφρονι φωτὶ ἔοικας is already published (odyssey-028, "since neither to a bad
  nor to a foolish man do you look like"), and a repeated line takes the same English. Kept; the
  clash between the table and odyssey-028 is the owner's to settle (changing both together).
- **250–251 "slaughtering"**: odyssey-083 prints the same two lines with `l` "sacrificing" (its own
  `i` says "slaughtered"). Pass 1's "slaughtering" follows the table row and the seven other shipped
  uses of ἱερεύω; kept. If strict identity with 083 is wanted, the outlier is 083's `l`.
- **261 καί μιν πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν** ("and to him a speech he said:", new-renderings.md): the same
  half-line is published four ways (odyssey-021 "to her spoke a word", -071 "and to him a speech
  uttered", -086 "and him with a word addressed", -098 "and to him spoke a word"), and the table's
  tmesis rows use "with a word addressed" or "uttered". The new rendering differs from all of them,
  and its stated reason for avoiding "spoke a word" does not mention them. Not changed (new-renderings.md
  is outside this pass's files); flagged for the owner to pick one of the four.
- **284 λώβης θυμαλγέος "insult"**: the row for λώβη (19.373) turns "insult" down, but the row
  specific to this phrase (λώβη θυμαλγής, 18.347) fixes "heart-paining insult" / "insult that pained
  the heart", and odyssey-091 has the line so. Kept.
- **218 υἷος ἐόντος "living"/"alive"**: the Greek says only "being"; kept because the shipped entry
  for ἐόντος already reads "being, alive" and the note states the Telemachus reading.
- **224 ὀΐομαι "I have in mind / think of"**: sense is context-taken; the note says the construction
  is loose. Kept (pass 1's reason stands).
- **275 ἐμπάζετο "did not take heed of"**: odyssey-086 renders the near-identical clause "he heeded
  not their words"; the table row (ἐμπάζεο, "take heed of") and the 086 `i` ("paid no heed") agree
  with ours. Kept.
- **201 doubled "none"; 262 "your wine"; 245 συνθεύσεται "run along"**: pass 1's reasons stand
  (renders οὔ τις … ἄλλος in Greek order; the wine just poured for him; the note and gloss now both
  say the sense is from context).
- **252 note on σπλάγχνα "tasted first in a sacrifice meal"** and **the remark that "wine mixed with water, which
  was the custom"**: cultural facts, not claims about other parts of the poem. Kept.
- **282 ἀνώγει**: the note says pluperfect used as imperfect; the shipped entry says "impf. 3 sg.".
  Compatible; the shipped entry is not rewritten.
- **Shipped entries with non-house words** (ὑπερμενέων "overweening", ὑπερφιάλοισι "overbearing,
  arrogant", σῖτον "bread", ἀθέσφατοι "agreeing with νύκτες"): old entries, which may only be
  broadened; left.
- **Pass 1 findings re-examined**: all of its 41 field edits re-read against the Greek; none reverted.
  The pass-1 statement that the table row for πάτερ ὦ ξεῖνε fixes the 199 wording was checked and is
  true (the row is at line 1021 of conventions.md).
